 Bafana’s qualification route demands and calculations 
 Nov 17, 2026 - 10:08 am
 By Lovemore Moyo 
 SA-National-Teams 
 The reality facing Bafana Bafana in meeting the minimal qualification expectations for the 2027 African Cup Of Nations (AFCON) finals has placed similar demands to what they did in the first round of fixtures in Group D. 
 Bafana have collected seven points so far in the first three matches and will go through with at least another seven points in the three games left.
 Three points for Bafana's taking
 Considering that three points against Eritrea in the last group match is expected, it is now up to Pitso Mosimane to determine where the other four points come from.
 READ| PSL hitman lights up international stage 
 The first and more doable option is to take all three points away in Kenya on Tuesday and then avoid defeat in Conakry against Guinea in March next year.
 Another point against the Harambee Stars will need Bafana to win in Conakry – a mountain climb option.
 Anything less than that will need calculations and favours tied to Kenya not giving away three points when they host Guinea. 
 So, the match at the Nyayo National Stadium suddenly carries three points wrapped in gold.
 Bafana must win.
 They need to win just like they have done on all their four previous visits to East Africa for AFCON qualifiers since being readmitted to FIFA.
 Whether by hook or crook, they need to have collected three points by the time they go to bed on Tuesday before preparing the four-hour flight back to Johannesburg on Wednesday.
 Failure to qualify for the AFCON finals will be catastrophic for Bafana as a top 10 ranked nation on the continent.
 The trickery of host nations in groups
 The Nations Cup finals now accommodate 24 countries, and so qualification should be standard for nations like South Africa.
 Unfortunately for Bafana, this qualification route has been cruel in that it guarantees Kenya their place at the finals as co-hosts and leaves South Africa and Guinea to battle it out for the second spot.
 READ: Bafana suffer rankings drop after Kenya draw 
 This is the same scenario in all groups with host nations – Group D (Kenya), Group H (Uganda), and Group L (Tanzania).
 Tunisia, Libya, and Botswana are fighting for one place in Group H, just like Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, and Madagascar in Group L.
